The image shows a close-up of a red tomato fruit surface with:
- Multiple dark, circular fungal structures with radiating setae (bristle-like projections)
- White mycelium visible in the center cluster
- Concentric ring patterns visible on the fruit skin
- Classic acervuli (spore-producing bodies) of Colletotrichum species

The dark, spiky/bristly acervuli with setae radiating outward on a ripe tomato fruit surface are the hallmark sign of Anthracnose (*Colletotrichum* spp.). This matches the description: "dark fungal structures visible in the center of spots," "concentric ring pattern," and "water-soaked and sunken lesions" on overripe tomatoes. No other class in the list produces this type of setose acervular fruiting body.
